what: Ralph Lauren designs and sells apparel, accessories, footwear, fragrance and home products under the Polo Ralph Lauren, Ralph Lauren Collection and related brands. It has spent years raising prices and cutting discounting.
customers: Consumers in North America, Europe and Asia, through its own stores and website and selected wholesale partners.
money: retail and wholesale across European markets
China, Japan and other Asian markets
moat: A brand built over almost sixty years around a consistent American aesthetic, with enough pricing power that it can walk away from discount channels.
risks: Apparel demand is discretionary and falls in a downturn
Tariffs on imported clothing raise costs
Chinese consumer demand for Western brands has been uneven
Counterfeiting and brand dilution are persistent issues
opportunities: Revenue grew about 15% last year with a 70% gross margin
Return on invested capital of 17% after years of reducing discounting
Asian revenue is growing much faster than North America
watch: Average unit retail price and Asian revenue growth.
